value.account:
WHAT I CHANGED
- orchestrator/state.py: optional RunState.result_persistence_profile (validated in __post_init__, omitted from to_dict when absent, never backfilled on load); StateManager.initialize(..., result_persistence_profile=); the four atomic eligible-pure transactions (begin/reuse/settle_success/settle_failure), delegating to visit-atomic helpers.
- New modules (each <500 lines): workflow/pure_replay_witness.py (error type, witness, exact shell build/validate, progress classification, RunState mutators), pure_replay_index.py (eligibility, binding-document typing, dependency index, topological order, _propagate_pure_ineligibility), pure_replay_surfaces.py (profile_conflict audit of steps/pure_bundle/private lineage/checkpoint records/restore payloads), pure_result_replay.py (PureReplayRuntime plus the importable re-exports named in the task, and automatic_result_persistence_profile).
- call_frame_state.py: load_existing_call_frame_read_only; malformed existing frames raise ValueError('existing call-frame state ...') before any directory or write; child managers get the same visit transactions. calls.py: a fresh, non-iterative child frame whose callee has frontend_kind == workflow_lisp selects the profile (existing frames are never backfilled; a fresh retry after a failed predecessor is new state so it selects it).
- outcomes.py: persist_step_result(..., eligible_pure_settlement=witness) settles the shell (or full failure/skip row) through the state manager, keeps the full result in memory, and hands the shell to the summary emitter.
- executor.py: provider observation manager now created at execute() start (not construction) and closed once; replay runtime built per scope; pre-prologue audit (profile_conflict raises, progress_witness_invalid is recorded as pure_result_replay_unavailable); one restart determination per resume, passed to ResumePlanner.determine_default_resume_decision(restart_node_id=...) (also added to the lexical-restore variant); eligible pure steps use begin/reuse + in-memory evaluation (no bundle read/write) + shell settlement; resume replays required pure values into an in-memory overlay (never durable) after default-resume decision; no checkpoint record is emitted for eligible pure steps.
- lexical_checkpoint_restore.py: restore payloads omit bindings sourced from eligible pure steps. lexical_checkpoint_default_resume.py: eligible pure points are filtered before unique-nearest selection; zero-record case returns VALIDATED_FRAME_ENTRY_REPLAY (validated_frame_entry_replay) or FAIL_CLOSED with lexical_default_resume_prior_boundary_not_restorable.
- CLI: run and resume --force-restart select the profile for typed compiled .orc; the force-restart path no longer writes the observability override into the source run (source state is byte-identical; verified).
- specs/state.md: new 'Derived Pure-Result Persistence Profile' section plus the field entry.
- Tests: tests/test_workflow_pure_result_replay{,_runtime,_surfaces}.py + tests/pure_replay_helpers.py. I changed two existing assertions in tests/test_provider_observation_workflow.py because they asserted construction-time manager creation, which the task reverses.

VERIFICATION
New tests plus the resume/state/subworkflow/lexical-checkpoint/pure-projection/observation suites: 440 passed. Real end-to-end checks: `python -m orchestrator run` on a .orc stores the shell and profile; `resume --force-restart` left the source state.json sha256-identical and the new root has the profile and requested observability; an interrupted materialize-view run resumed to the same outputs through VALIDATED_FRAME_ENTRY_REPLAY with the effect not re-run. A full-suite run showed only failures that also fail on a pristine `git archive HEAD` copy (sandbox: unix-socket path length, tmux, provider isolation, nanobragg, wcc_characterization, key migrations, etc.); I did not let the final slow tail (lean-pilot parity tests) finish.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED / DISCARDED
- Doing the default-resume decision before replay: discarded because durable-input errors must surface as pure_result_replay_unavailable; instead replay runs first against the durable (shell) state and the overlay is projected into the in-memory state only after the decision.
- Keeping eligible pure points as checkpoint candidates with empty payloads: discarded (the spec filters them); a payload-less node-local record is treated as absent only under the profile and only with no diagnostics, so unsafe pending-effect records still fail closed.
- Adding a mapping/attr hybrid step view for evaluate_node rather than guessing one signature.

NOT COVERED / UNCERTAIN (please review)
- Signatures I had to guess: evaluate_node(step_view, overlay_state) where step_view is a dict that also exposes node attributes; resolve_bundle_path(node)->Path|None; scope_kind accepts only 'root' (every bundle is its own root scope; expected_scope is the requested kind, actual_scope the bundle's) so 'call_frame' always mismatches; PureReplayRuntime always indexes with scope 'root'.
- 'Durable owner' for frame-entry replay is interpreted as validated bound-input leaves plus exact witnesses; I did not model other owners. 'Unbound text' is only a literal fully matching ${...}.
- profile_conflict propagates as an exception out of execute() (no state write); other replay failures are recorded run errors.
- Not exercised by tests: iteration-owned child frames keeping the historical profile, imported-callee index scoping in a real multi-bundle program, and a multi-effect program with pure steps interleaved between committed effects (the compiler folded my sample's pure work into one terminal node).
- Pyright warns about fixture re-imports in the new test modules (standard pytest pattern).
